primary_source.citation: Seonglae Cho et al., Automata from Agent Traces: Failure and Next-Step Prediction for Long-Horizon LLM Agents, arXiv:2608.23670, 2026-08-24

verified_findings.fsm_replay_fitness: The author source reports near-perfect held-out trace replay: tau2 retail 0.998, telecom 1.000, and SWE-agent 0.997/0.998 in the reported settings.
verified_findings.failure_prediction: Per-state/transition features reach AUROC up to 0.941; ATBench reports 0.894 and repeated-CV mean 0.864 +/- 0.024.
verified_findings.online_monitor: For SWE-agent specifically, the reported online structural monitor has precision 0.859, recall 0.955, and fires after roughly 32% of trace completion.
verified_findings.context_ablation: On tau2-bench retail, minimal/local projected workflow context reaches 65.1% top-1 next-action accuracy while full-FSM context is about 52.2%; additional multi-step graph context is reported at 49.2%.

scope_corrections: The 85.9% precision, 95.5% recall, and roughly 32% trace-completion figures are SWE-agent-specific, not a universal result over all twelve datasets.

The full-FSM-versus-minimal-context underperformance is a tau2-bench retail ablation. It is evidence that wholesale workflow materialization can interfere in that tested setting, not a theorem that full history is generally worse.

Replay fitness near 0.997-1.000 concerns the induced FSM's fit to observed/held-out trace-prefix language; it is not proof that the FSM recovered the agent's full hidden generating workflow or true rules.
Action extraction and FSM construction are method-specific and can degrade for sparse or weakly sequential action spaces.
This audit verified the author-reported primary-source values but did not independently rerun the code or recompute them from raw trajectories.
